core_conclusion: The greatest cognitive bias in translation lies in Buddhist-Daoist terms such as 'Mind-Monkey and Will-Horse', 'True Samadhi Fire', and 'Victorious Fighting Buddha' — English readers can hardly perceive the cultivation metaphor in the dharma names 'Wukong/Wujing'. East Asian countries amplify different elements: Japan leans toward bishōnen and hot-bloodedness, South Korea toward romance and education, and China's local adaptations stay most faithful to the original, though a dark style has emerged in recent years.
